P09 clean SDK consumer conformance: a standalone, builtins-only clean consumer fixture (tests/fixtures/versioned-sdk-clean-consumer.mjs) copies P08's real versioned SDK distribution payload into a temp directory, empties the environment, and validates the distribution version, module path, manifest shape, module file existence and the exact recomputed SHA-256 before importing it; test-verified; no npm publish/release

P10 app-core: an app-owned Customer app-core public-SDK consumer boundary (consumers/customer-app-core/customer-app-core.mjs, CUSTOMER_APP_CORE_MANIFEST plus createCustomerAppCore) that composes a P08-generated public action SDK module only through its public contract surface at an exact SDK-derived coordinate, fails closed on a missing/malformed/wrong-coordinate SDK or a missing/near-match customer:core capability grant (default-deny), and exposes no schema/adapter/CRUD/Surface/UI/host/release/readiness behavior; test-verified

P11 app-owned customer schema: a pure, zero-import, application-owned customer_records schema and validator contract (consumers/customer-app-core/customer-records-schema.mjs, CUSTOMER_RECORDS_SCHEMA plus canonicalizeCustomerRecord) that deep-freezes its six-field/index/RLS/runtime-grant descriptor and canonicalizes/validates an exact-six-key record fail-closed, with no SQL, migration, adapter, CRUD, or cutover behavior; test-verified

P12 app-owned adapter: an application-owned, query-injected customer_records adapter (consumers/customer-app-core/customer-records-adapter.mjs, createCustomerRecordsAdapter) that canonicalizes a record against the P11 schema/validator contract, requires a matching tenantId, and issues exactly one parameterized INSERT via a caller-supplied query function, with no real database connection, migration, cutover, or CRUD read/update/delete behavior; test-verified

P13 data cutover and rollback: a frozen, default-legacy customer_records data cutover controller (consumers/customer-app-core/customer-data-cutover.mjs, createCustomerDataCutover) that gates a compatibility-checked switch of activeWriter to the P12 adapter behind one BEGIN/mfk_begin_tenant_context/P12-adapter-insert/COMMIT transaction with rollback-on-failure, plus rollback()/close(), with no live traffic moved and no app-core wiring; test-verified

P14 app-core cutover composition (P14a): consumers/customer-app-core/customer-app-core.mjs adds createCustomerAppCoreWithPersistence, reusing createCustomerAppCore's public-SDK-contract and customer:core fail-closed validation unchanged and composing a real createCustomerDataCutover from injected cutoverOptions into a frozen {sdkCoordinate, status, persistence} result, default-legacy, no automatic cutover; test-verified

P14 app-owned persistence parity (P14b/P14e): consumers/customer-app-core/customer-persistence-adapter.mjs (createCustomerPersistenceAdapter) fail-closed validates tenantId/audit/transactionalOutbox/idempotency metadata before any query, delegates the unchanged P12 adapter for the canonical customer_records insert, writes audit_log and transactional_outbox with the same SQL/param shape as the Kernel's own postgres-write-envelope-write.mjs, and maps the pg 23505 transactional_outbox_tenant_dedup_key violation to a new CustomerIdempotencyConflictError; the P13 cutover's application branch calls this adapter, synthesizing Kernel-parity default metadata only when the caller supplies none at all and fail-closed rejecting a partial explicit metadata set; test-verified against real PostgreSQL 16

P14 transitional Kernel ownership cleanup and legacy adapter retirement (P14c/P14d1/P14d2a/P14d2b): tools/check-kernel-persistence-ownership.mjs retires the combined transitionalInKernel manifest record fail-closed, src/adapters/postgres-write-envelope-write.mjs now directly owns IdempotencyConflictError/isDuplicateIdempotencyFingerprintError/checkPreparedChangeSet/checkTenantId moved verbatim out of the transitional src/adapters/postgres-commit-adapter.mjs, the legacy postgres-commit-adapter.mjs test suite was retired, and the transitional src/adapters/postgres-commit-adapter.mjs file itself is now physically removed from the repository; test-verified

P14 isolated real PostgreSQL 16 proof (P14e): tests/postgres-unit-of-work-write-envelope.test.mjs exercises createCustomerAppCoreWithPersistence against one real shared PostgreSQL container across three strong scenarios — legacy default touches no database, a real cutover plus application insert commits one row per table with a frozen canonical record, a repeated idempotency fingerprint is rejected with rollback to exactly one row per table, and a partial explicit parity metadata set is fail-closed rejected with zero rows written in any table; test-verified, no live entrypoint, host, Surface, relay, release, deploy or automatic cutover trigger wired

P15 Customer module typed API: consumers/customer-app-core/customer-module-api.mjs (createCustomerModuleApi, CUSTOMER_MODULE_API_MANIFEST) composes the P14 createCustomerAppCoreWithPersistence handle behind a frozen, fail-closed customer.create@1 manifest (operations ["recordCustomer"]), validating every recordCustomer call's actionSpec via the P08 SDK, canonicalizing the record via P11's canonicalizeCustomerRecord, cross-checking tenant/audit/outbox correlation before ever touching the injected legacyInsert, and returning a frozen {ok:true, record}; test-verified 5/5 (tests/kernel-customer-module-api-p15.test.mjs, PR #116 with a passing CI run), no live entrypoint, host or Surface wiring

P16 separate Surface/UI projection: consumers/customer-app-core/customer-surface.mjs (createCustomerSurface, CUSTOMER_SURFACE_MANIFEST) composes a real, ready P15 customerModuleApi handle behind a frozen idle/submitting/saved/rejected UI projection, exposing submit/retry with single-flight submission, sanitized rejection (CUSTOMER_SURFACE_SUBMIT_REJECTED alert code only, never reason/message/stack/Error) and exact-args retry; test-verified 4/4 (tests/kernel-customer-surface-p16.test.mjs, PR #118 with a passing CI run), no DOM, host, DB, relay or readiness-flag change

P17 installable ASGI host adapters: host/pyproject.toml makes host/ an installable, offline-buildable pure-Python distribution via uv_build (module-root="", module-name="python_asgi"), package metaframer-kernel-asgi-host version 0.1.0a1, requires-python >=3.12, no dependencies, console-script metaframer-kernel-customer-host = python_asgi.create_customer_host_cli:main, whose create_customer_host_cli.main requires an explicit --runner (uvicorn or hypercorn, no default) plus a literal -- separator followed by a non-empty application-side JS command, failing closed (parser.error, no dispatch) on a missing --runner, a missing -- separator, or an empty command after it; host/python_asgi/__init__.py now publicly re-exports exactly three names — StdioJsAsgiBridge, create_customer_app, run_create_customer_host — importable with no uvicorn/hypercorn/fastapi/django installed or imported at package-import time; test-verified 3/3 (tests/kernel-python-asgi-installable-package-p17.test.mjs, PR #120 with a passing CI run), packaging/installability contract only, no listener started, no live entrypoint/host wiring, no production/release claim

P18 fenced outbox relay run-once: db/metaframer_kernel_db/outbox_relay.py's run_outbox_relay_once(sqlalchemy_url, tenant_id, deliver, *, limit, lease_seconds) — no defaults on limit/lease_seconds, both required keyword-only — composes the existing S1 substrate's claim_batch/publish_claim/release_claim primitives into one single-pass drain: claims up to limit rows under a lease in its own transaction, offers each row to the caller-supplied deliver callback, and in a second, fresh transaction per outcome calls publish_claim on a True return and release_claim (not a plain retry) on any falsy return or raised exception, fencing a stale claimant's late token to zero rows; returns a frozen OutboxRelayResult(published, failed) — two id tuples, no remaining/count field; test-verified against real PostgreSQL 16 across 3 scenarios (db/tests/test_outbox_relay_lifecycle.py, PR #122 with a passing CI run) — a clean drain publishes every row and a second call finds nothing left, a failed delivery is released (not published) and the same id stays retryable, and a stale claimant's late token is fenced after the relay reclaims and publishes; run-once only, no scheduler, no retry-interval loop, no dead-letter queue, no live entrypoint/host wiring, no production/release claim

P19 observed outbox relay SLO: db/metaframer_kernel_db/observability.py's run_observed_outbox_relay_once wraps P18's run_outbox_relay_once with a RelaySlo threshold and emits exactly one structured outbox_relay.batch_completed event per call carrying batch duration and failure-rate measurements plus a RelaySlo verdict (green/red on duration and on failure-rate independently), test-verified against real PostgreSQL 16 across exactly 3 scenarios (db/tests/test_outbox_relay_observability_slo.py, PR #124 with a passing CI run 32970268485) — a clean drain and a second empty pass are both SLO green, a partial failure preserves P18's publish/release outcomes and goes failure-rate red without leaking exception detail, and a deterministically slow but fully successful drain is only latency red; single-pass observed run only, no exporter, no dashboard, no alert transport, no scheduler/consumer-loop/retry policy/DLQ around the relay, no live entrypoint/host wiring, no production/release claim

P20 performance baseline: db/metaframer_kernel_db/performance.py's summarize_relay_performance(samples) computes a deterministic, ambient-clock-free RelayPerformanceBaseline over caller-supplied RelayPerformanceSample values — nearest-rank p95/p99 duration seconds, published/failed totals, summed measured wall_clock_seconds and a seconds_per_published proxy, a sorted per-tenant p95 breakdown, and a measured fairness_ratio (min/max tenant p95) — test-verified against real PostgreSQL 16 across exactly 3 scenarios (db/tests/test_outbox_relay_performance_baseline.py, PR #126 with a passing CI run 32982906594); pure summarization only, no calibrated SLA/threshold, no scheduler, retry, DLQ, exporter, dashboard, live host, optimizer, load generator or dollar-cost claim
